findings.title: Anyone can read other people's Habit records
findings.text: Which records it uses comes straight from the request, and nothing checks who is asking. Changing a value in the request gets someone else's data.

findings.title: Stripe secret key is sent to the browser
findings.text: lib/stripe.ts contains a Stripe secret key and is imported by code that runs in the browser (/pro). Anyone can open developer tools and copy it.

evidence.code: export const stripe = new Stripe("sk_live_DEMO…");

findings.title: Accepts messages without checking who sent them
findings.text: This webhook changes the database (User) but never verifies a signature. Anyone who finds the address can send a fake message.

findings.title: Open to anyone, no login check
findings.text: This route uses the database without checking a login. That can be intended (sign-up, public data), so it's listed for review, not as a bug.

findings.title: If an unresolved address fails, the request fails after data was saved
findings.text: The call to an unresolved address isn't wrapped in error handling and happens after the User write. A failure there shows the user an error even though the record already exists.

limits: Reads TypeScript/JavaScript structure only. It does not run the code.

Understands Next.js routes and pages, Prisma, Drizzle (pgTable/mysqlTable/sqliteTable schemas, select/insert/update/delete, joins and db.query with `with`), Supabase, and the service packages in its list. Other libraries show up as plain code, not as parts.
Calls made through require(), dynamic import(), or values passed around as arguments may be missed.
Regex-style middleware matchers are not evaluated.
